title: Why Saffron Costs More Than Any Spice On Earth
note: The queued story saffron-red-gold-myth, made as the third 3D short. One number at most per beat; the closing says why you care. Every claim is in 'sources' with the source's own wording.
lines: Saffron costs more than any spice on Earth, and it's all picked by hand.
Each purple crocus holds just three tiny red threads. You need a whole basket of flowers for one pinch.
Every flower is picked by hand, then every thread is pulled out by hand, for hours on end.
And it's a race. The flowers open at dawn and start to wilt as the day goes on.
So that tiny jar isn't pricey for the spice. You're paying for all those hands.

sources.says: At US$5,000 per kg or higher, saffron has long been the world's costliest spice by weight.

sources.claim: It is picked by hand; the price comes from the labour
sources.says: The high retail value of saffron is maintained on world markets because of labour-intensive harvesting methods. Forty hours of labour are needed to pick 150,000 flowers.

sources.claim: Each crocus holds three red threads (stigmas)
sources.says: a style ... branches into three ... Each prong terminates with a vivid crimson stigma

sources.claim: A basket of flowers for one pinch (about 150 flowers per gram)
sources.says: roughly 150 flowers yield 1 g (1/32 oz) of dry saffron threads

sources.claim: The flowers open at dawn and wilt as the day goes on
sources.says: after blossoming at dawn, flowers quickly wilt as the day passes. All plants bloom within a window of one or two weeks.

sets_why: the shop where you pay, the field where it grows, the room where the threads come out, the field at dawn, back to the shop
ideas: a pile of cash for one tiny jar
three threads barely move the gram scale
the clock spins through the hours as he plucks
the rising sun closes the flowers toward him
the tiny jar balances a heap of flowers
storyboard: 1 hook (store): Data at a checkout counter holds ONE tiny glass jar of red saffron threads up to us; he sets it down and slides a thick stack of cash across the counter for it, then another, the bills piling up beside the tiny jar; he looks back at us, eyebrows up.

2 threads (crocus_field): a field of purple crocus flowers; Data holds ONE flower up close to us, its three bright red threads sticking out; he pulls the threads and drops them on the pan of a little gram scale beside him and the needle barely twitches; he looks at us, unimpressed.

3 by hand (sorting_room): a farmhouse table heaped with purple flowers; Data pulls the red threads out of one flower after another with his own hands into a small dish; on the wall behind him a clock's hands spin round and round and the window light goes from day to night.

4 the race (crocus_field at dawn): the sun rises over the hills behind the field and the open purple flowers fold shut in a wave rolling toward Data; he grabs flowers into his basket as fast as he can before the wave reaches him.

5 payoff (store): the checkout counter again with a balance scale: the tiny jar alone on one pan; Data tips his basket of purple flowers onto the other pan, a big heap, and only then does the scale level out; he turns to us: that's what's in the jar.
